title: Interleaving String
prompt:
Return `true` if `s3` can be formed by interleaving `s1` and `s2`, meaning every character of both is used and each string's characters stay in their original order.

**Example**: `s1 = "aabcc"`, `s2 = "dbbca"`, `s3 = "aadbbcbcac"` → `true`; with `s3 = "aadbbbaccc"` → `false`.

**Constraints**: `0 <= s1.length, s2.length <= 100`, `0 <= s3.length <= 200`.
hints: Always taking the next character from whichever string matches can go wrong when both match. After producing some prefix of s3, what two numbers fully describe where you are?
Let dp[i][j] = the first i characters of s1 and the first j of s2 can form the first i+j of s3. The last character came from either s1 or s2. If the lengths don't add up, return false.
`dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j] && s1.charAt(i-1) == s3.charAt(i+j-1)) || (dp[i][j-1] && s2.charAt(j-1) == s3.charAt(i+j-1));` Seed row and column 0 from a single string's prefix.

solution.explanation: Any interleaving of s1[0..i) and s2[0..j) ends with a character from one of them, following a valid interleaving of the shorter prefixes, so the OR of those two cases is exactly right. Where greedy has to guess when both strings match, the table tries both. O(m·n) time and space.
